obligation: PHMSA immediate telephonic notice of an incident
trigger: An incident under 191.3: a release of gas with death, in-patient injury, property damage of $122,000 or more (inflation-adjusted), or unintentional loss of 3 million cubic feet or more; OR an event that is significant in the judgment of the operator (191.3 paragraph (3)). A cyber-caused shutdown of the transmission line may be judged significant even with no release
deadline: At the earliest practicable moment following discovery, but no later than one hour after confirmed discovery
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the Operations Manager decides whether the event is significant; default is to report a cyber-caused shut-in or curtailment of the line

obligation: PHMSA revision or confirmation of the telephonic notice
trigger: An incident reported under 191.5(a)
deadline: Within 48 hours after confirmed discovery, to the extent practicable: revise or confirm estimates of product released, fatalities and injuries, and other significant facts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if a 191.5 notice was made

obligation: PHMSA written incident report (transmission)
trigger: An incident required to be reported under 191.5
deadline: As soon as practicable but not more than 30 days after detection; supplemental report when more information is obtained (191.15(d))
notify: PHMSA via the electronic portal (Form PHMSA F 7100.2)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if a 191.5 notice was made

obligation: FPSC telephonic notice of accidents
trigger: An event involving the release of gas from a pipeline that caused death or hospitalization, required taking any segment of transmission pipeline out of service, resulted in ignition, caused $10,000 or more in property damage, or was significant in the operator's judgment. Not required for (b) or (c) events caused solely by planned or routine maintenance or construction (25-12.084(2))
deadline: At the earliest practicable moment following discovery
notify: Florida Public Service Commission (gas safety staff)
applies_at_this_tier: Only if gas is released. A precautionary shut-in with no release does not trigger this rule; make a courtesy call to FPSC gas safety staff anyway

obligation: Emergency notice to public safety answering points and officials
trigger: A gas pipeline emergency, including a shutdown that creates a hazard or a loss of supply that local officials must plan for
deadline: No fixed clock; notify and coordinate as the emergency plan provides. Immediate notice after a notification of potential rupture (192.615(a)(8))
notify: 9-1-1 center, the city fire department, and the county emergency manager along the route
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the shut-in or event creates an emergency (for example loss of supply to the municipal system)

obligation: TSA pipeline cybersecurity incident reporting
trigger: Cybersecurity incident at a TSA-designated owner/operator
deadline: As soon as practicable, but no later than 72 hours after identifying a cybersecurity incident (IC Surface-2025-01 recommends earlier notice to TSA for significant incidents)
notify: CISA Central (cisa.gov/report or 844-729-2472); CISA shares with TSA
applies_at_this_tier: No - not TSA-designated (P03 section 1.1). Kept as a readiness reference; the voluntary CISA report below follows the same content

obligation: Voluntary cyber incident report to CISA
citation: CISA incident reporting system (voluntary for this company)
trigger: Ransomware or other significant cyber incident
deadline: Voluntary; target within 72 hours of identification (the SD 01G clock, for readiness)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary; also supports OFAC mitigation if a payment is considered

obligation: Voluntary report to the FBI
trigger: Ransomware or extortion
deadline: Voluntary; as early as possible
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransomware payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons; strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals
trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents (employee and former employee records in HR or payroll files)
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach (the 15-day good-cause extension in 501.171(3)(a) applies only to this notice to individuals)
notify: Affected Florida residents (employees and former employees)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if employee personal information was accessed

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds records on far fewer than 500 people; count before deciding

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at one time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: No - far fewer than 1,000 people

obligation: Third-party agent notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: A vendor that maintains personal information for the company (payroll service, MSP, accounting SaaS) has a breach
deadline: No later than 10 days following the determination of the breach
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - track in contracts

obligation: State data breach notification
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of state residents (definitions vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where the state requires it; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Check residency of affected employees; apply the law of each state where they live

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident report / ransom payment report (PROPOSED - not yet in effect)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment by a covered entity
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours after reasonable belief a covered cyber incident occurred; 24 hours after ransom payment disbursed
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published at approval (2026-09-15). Even as proposed, the company is far below the SBA size standard and is not a pipeline required to report to TSA (proposed 226.2(b)(14)(iv), as corrected by FR Doc. 2024-12084). Recheck when final

obligation: NERC CIP-008-6 R4 Reportable Cyber Security Incident notification
trigger: Reportable Cyber Security Incident at a registered entity with high or medium impact BES Cyber Systems
deadline: (High/medium impact BES Cyber Systems and associated EACMS) Within 1 hour after determination of a Reportable Cyber Security Incident; by end of next calendar day for an attempt to compromise an applicable system; updates within 7 calendar days of new information
applies_at_this_tier: No - not a NERC-registered entity; no Bulk Electric System assets

obligation: Form DOE-417 Electric Emergency Incident and Disturbance Report (formerly OE-417; includes cyber events)
citation: Form DOE-417, OMB-approved ICR 202402-1901-002 (expires 2027-05-31); mandatory under 15 U.S.C. 772(b)
trigger: Electric utilities and other listed entities file when their Balancing Authority does not. Criteria 2-3 (Reportable Cyber Security Incident; cyber event interrupting operations) and 11-12 (cyber event that could affect reliability; loss of service to over 50,000 customers for 1 hour or more), among others
deadline: Within 1 hour (criteria 2-3), within 6 hours (criteria 11-12); final report within 72 hours
notify: DOE Office of Cybersecurity, Energy Security, and Emergency Response (CESER)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company has no electric operations

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d) (Section 889); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

obligation: Kaspersky covered article discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies a covered article (Kaspersky Lab hardware, software, or services) in use or delivered
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

obligation: Customer and upstream pipeline notices
citation: Firm transportation contracts and the interconnect operating agreement (contractual)
trigger: Manual operation, curtailment, or shut-in affecting deliveries or receipts
deadline: Per contract; before any planned curtailment, then every 4 hours
notify: Municipal gas system, ceramic tile plant, food processing plant, and the upstream interstate pipeline
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: SCADA vendor and MSP security incident notice to the company (inbound)
citation: SCADA vendor contract and MSP contract (contractual)
trigger: Security incident at the vendor that affects the company's tenant, devices, or data
deadline: None in current contracts; 24 hours sought in the security addendum by 2026-12-31 (POAM-011)
notify: The company (Office Manager and Operations Manager)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident, extortion demand, or data theft
deadline: Per policy: prompt notice through the 24x7 breach hotline, before hiring outside firms; use panel counsel and forensics
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal
